newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro wants to bring Web to Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro wants to bring Web to Wall St.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc said it will Monday introduce a new Java-based architecture for building and deploying Web-based financial service products.

The new architecture, dubbed Sun Connect, allows companies to develop products for use on any computer platform and will support emerging specifications for online transactions, including the Open Financial Exchange (OFX) and other protocols, Sun representatives said.
Sun will demonstrate an OFX server running live in conjunction with a major online brokerage firm at the Securities Industry Association meeting in New York, the company said.

Sun Connect is a computer development environment using components entirely of the Java language which offers data security and rapid development of applications designed to run on virtually any computer system.
Sun is expected to announce a number of organizations in technology and financial services that are working on the Sun Connect architecture, including BEA Systems and New Era of Networks Inc.

Meca Software LLC, a consortium owned by Bank America Corp, NationsBank Corp, First Bank Systems Inc, Fleet Financial Group, the Royal Bank of Canada and The New England, said it is also planning to build Java-based applications on Sun Connect.
BEA helped enable Sun Connect to link with older transaction systems using BEA's transactional management product known as Tuxedo.

The Sun Connect framework will include Sun's Java Tool Kit and Java Studio as well as other software application tools, the company said. Pricing and availability of the tools was not immediately available.
